title: Harness Capability Profile (v1)
description: What the harness that will replay these plans can actually do. frameladder plans against its own interpreter, where every variable is settable and every operation replayable; a real harness is narrower and projects a plan down to what it supports, dropping the rest. A plan that depended on a dropped value still runs and simply means nothing. This document turns that projection into a constraint the planner can honour before it spends any budget. Sections may be omitted; an absent section states no constraint rather than an empty one.

program.description: Program the profile describes, for the harness's own bookkeeping.

ordinal_source.description: Who counted the `ordinal` fields below. Only "frameladder" is read as an identity; anything else (or absence) means the ordinals are the harness's own and are used as a hint at most. This is not pedantry: frameladder numbers a decision by its statement position within its paragraph, while a harness may number per (paragraph, kind), so their third IF is frameladder's ordinal 3 -- a number that usually exists and usually names a different decision. Measured on the CardDemo corpus, taking foreign ordinals at face value pointed 1251 of 1644 targets at the wrong decision, silently. Identify decisions by `condition` and `line` instead; those are properties of the COBOL that both sides read off the same file.

injectable_variables.description: Entry-state variables the harness can set. A binding on anything else makes a plan unrepresentable. Omit the section entirely to state no constraint; an empty array means the harness can inject nothing.

replayable_operations.description: External operations the harness can mock, keyed the way frameladder keys them: READ:FILE, OPEN-INPUT:FILE, CALL:PGM, EXEC:SQL:SELECT, EXEC:CICS:READ. Mode is part of the identity because it decides the outcome.

fields.description: Payload fields this operation can set. Omit for no restriction.

matches_on_state.description: Whether the harness can select an outcome by inspecting program state, rather than only replaying an ordered list. A plan tells two invocations of one verb apart by a discriminator -- 'the READ whose key is X returns not-found' -- and a harness that cannot match on state will deliver those in order and ignore the condition, which is a different test from the one planned. Omit if you do not know; omission is reported, not treated as a refusal.

max_outcomes.description: Longest outcome series the harness can replay for this operation. 0 or absent means no stated limit. A read loop needs a series, not a value.

aliases.description: Other names the harness answers to for this same operation. Case and punctuation are already handled -- EXEC:CICS:READ, `EXEC CICS READ` and `exec/cics/read` all match without an alias -- so this is for the rest, where the harness knows a file by a DD name, a table name or a handle the COBOL never mentions. That mapping cannot be derived from the source by anyone, which is why the harness states it rather than having it guessed.

uncovered_directions.description: The work list. Targeting these rather than deep paragraphs is what stops a plan succeeding on code that was already covered. Identify each decision by `paragraph` plus `condition` and/or `line`: those are read off the COBOL, so both sides derive the same value from the same file. `ordinal` is accepted but is only an identity when `ordinal_source` is "frameladder" -- see that field for why a foreign ordinal is worse than no ordinal. An entry that gives only a paragraph is honoured by targeting every decision in it, which costs planning budget rather than correctness. Run `frameladder <program> directions --capability <file>` to see exactly how a work list resolved before spending a run on it.

condition.description: The decision's condition as written in the source. The most reliable identifier there is: spelling differences (IS EQUAL TO against =, quote style, case, whitespace, a leading IF, outer parentheses, a trailing period) are all normalised away before comparison.

line.description: Source line of the decision. Narrows a condition that appears more than once in one paragraph. Not sufficient alone when COPY expansion puts several decisions on one line -- then every decision on it is targeted.

kind.description: Aliases are accepted: EVALUATE and SEARCH resolve to WHEN, PERFORM UNTIL / PERFORM VARYING to LOOP, AT END / INVALID KEY to PHRASE. A kind that matches nothing in the paragraph is ignored rather than treated as a claim the paragraph lacks it.

probe_id.description: The harness's own id for this direction, echoed back untouched on anything derived from it, so results can be joined without either side adopting the other's identity scheme.

direction.description: Which way. Accepts a boolean, or T/F, Y/N, taken/not-taken, then/else, match/nomatch. Absent means the whole decision is open and both directions are planned -- which is right, because picking one would be a guess that surfaces later as a witness on the direction nobody wanted.

attempts.description: What happened when the harness ran earlier plans, against the real compiled program. `first_missing_frame` is the valuable field: the run demonstrably reproduces the frame before it, so that frame is a far better place to plan from than the entry paragraph.
